fisc_categories.I: Invading and disrupting native plant communities in Florida.
fisc_categories.II: Increasing in number or range, but not yet changing native plant communities.

species.id_tips: Low cycad with stiff, dark green, feather-like fronds and rust-brown seed cones. Only host plant of the atala butterfly.
Big round leathery leaves, often with red veins. Hanging clusters of grape-like fruit. Common on the coast.
Rounded glossy leaves, often with a small notch at the tip. A popular native hedge.
Fan palm, usually low and sprawling, with sharp saw teeth along the leaf stalks. Green or silver forms.
Florida's state tree. Large fan leaves on smooth, toothless stalks, with criss-cross leaf bases ('boots') on the trunk.
Leaves in whorls of 3, often with reddish veins. Tubular red-orange flowers that hummingbirds and butterflies visit.
Very glossy opposite leaves with deep, 'quilted' veins. Small white flowers and red berries.
Soft, toothed opposite leaves. Tight clusters of bright purple berries ringing the stems in late summer and fall.
Shiny copper-red bark that peels in thin papery sheets. Compound leaves with 3 to 7 leaflets.
Arching prop roots over water, thick glossy opposite leaves, and long pencil-shaped seedlings hanging from branches.
Sprawling groundcover with rough, triangular leaves. Yellow sunflowers with a dark brown-purple center.
Long arching fronds of many small leaflets. Its roots have no round tubers.
Short (usually under 2 ft), hairy plant with oval leaves. Lavender flowers sit right against the stem in the leaf joints.
Compound leaves with 3 to 13 leaflets on a reddish, often winged stalk. Crushed leaves smell like turpentine or pepper. Bright red berries in winter. Related to poison ivy: the sap can irritate skin.
Thick, spongy, papery white bark that peels in layers. Stiff lance-shaped leaves with parallel veins and white bottlebrush flowers.
Not a real pine. Drooping, jointed, needle-like green twigs and small woody cones. Common on beaches and canal banks.
A fern that climbs as a vine, with small paired leaflets. Forms thick curtains that smother trees in wetlands.
Compound leaves with blunt, leathery leaflets. Orange inner bark (the 'carrot'). Yellow-orange seed capsules that split to show black seeds.
Twining vine with large heart-shaped leaves and arching veins. Grows potato-like bulbils in the leaf joints.
Curved, sickle-shaped 'leaves' with parallel veins. Pods twist into tight coils. Yellow flower spikes.
Shiny leaves, pinkish new growth, pale pink flowers and berries that ripen from red to glossy black.
Tall (up to 3 ft) with purplish stems and long, narrow leaves. Purple trumpet flowers on stalks. Some sold cultivars are sterile; the seeding kind spreads fast.
Leaves of 7 to 16 long glossy leaflets spread like an umbrella. Red flower spikes that look like octopus arms. Often grows on other trees.
Glossy, fleshy leaves, often with 3 lobes. Yellow-orange daisies with a yellow (not dark) center. Roots wherever stems touch the ground.
Looks almost the same as the native Boston fern from above. Pull one up: round, fuzzy, grape-sized tubers on the roots mean it's this invasive one.
